records.name: 石制小刀
records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one standalone inventory tool sprite for FlatWorld, a 2D survival sandbox in which people build technology from nothing.
Primary request: REDRAW ONLY THE ONE SUBJECT DESCRIBED BELOW.
Image 1 is ONLY the approved coarse-pixel style anchor: match its very large square pixel clusters and spare shading; do not depict a shovel. Image 2, if present, is ONLY the old material/function identity reference, never copy its extra objects or its layout.
Style: low-saturation realistic retro pixel art, roughly 48 x 48 logical pixel appearance enlarged with nearest-neighbor hard square steps. Deliberately chunky and simple, 12 to 20 total muted colors, two or three tones per material, flat large facets, no dense microtexture, no smooth or antialiased edges, no dithering, no tiny fine highlights. Upper-left light, minimal dark outline.
Composition: exactly one complete isolated object, centered on a square genuinely transparent alpha canvas, at least 13% empty space on every side. Short handle lower-left, working tip upper-right at about a 45-degree diagonal. Large readable silhouette. No background, no ground, no cast shadow, no label, no text, no hands, no people, no extra item.
World/style constraints: obvious handmade early technology; asymmetrical chipped or hand-forged material and a crooked roughly carved branch handle. For assembled tools make the structural blade-to-handle attachment clearly visible: THREE OR FOUR WIDE coarse tan plant-fiber cord or rawhide turns wrapped across the actual attachment, one simple large knot or cross-lashing, binding has a real fixing purpose and is not merely a decorative grip. Big pixel rope shapes only, no microscopic woven detail. No modern factory shapes, no machined socket, no screws, no pristine mirror polish, no ornate fantasy decoration.
Subject: One short primitive STONE KNIFE. Broad tapered gray stone flake blade with an irregular sharp pointed tip, only THREE large slate-gray flake facets, slightly asymmetrical edges. Short unpolished brown wooden handle. The blade tang sits inside the split top of the wooden handle, secured by 3 broad straw-colored cord bands across the join and ONE conspicuous crossed binding knot at the blade base. Stone must read as matte gray stone, not steel. Blade takes about 58 percent of the length; recognizable knife rather than arrowhead, axe or spear.
